title: Q
review: Absolutely haunting. Of powapowa-p's discography, this song always makes it into my playlist the most, and it always evokes complicated emotions. The classic rock combined with the light glockenspiel illustrate an innocent childlike angst, followed by a form of quiet resignation. We will never know the meaning of the title, whether it is a homophone for the japanese word for "suffering", whether Q stands for question reflecting mental turbulence, or both. In the case of the latter, knowledge of the answer is haunting, for it illustrates a tragic resolve.

title: ワンダー
review: r-906 has done it again, but this time with a new retro, disco vibe (and catchy chorus). I sorta get the vibe that the theme of the song is escapism, calling to an upbeat backrooms-esque aesthetic. In a way this goes hand-in-hand with Fisher's hauntology, the feeling of being trapped in time long past.

title: ray (超かぐや姫！ Version)
review: Movie version of an old Bump of Chicken song, also one of those songs that got my to actually go and watch the source. Usually don't care much for covers in anime, but this one seemed to capture a certain energy not captured by the original (and prosekai version). Before watching, only knowing the context of the original Kaguya-hime story, I got the impression that this song was a sort of optimistic masking of some a sad departure. After watching the movie, it's immediately recontextualized as a clear celebration. Simple song, but quality storytelling.

title: 君が僕を嗤う日
review: Beautiful cover of a song from an producer that wasn't on my radar. Falls in a "bittersweet" type of song nodding towards a sort of nostalgia. The pen scratches in the quiet last verse is absolute ASMR, juxtaposed directly with the high wpm singing in the chorus, it evokes a sort of shift from sweet remembrance to a reluctant distance (temporal, spatial, or interperonal, lots of room for interpretation).

title: かなしばりに遭ったら
review: A well performed cover that captures much of the texture and tone from avaraya's original. Stilted, syncopated vocals with distortion effects to make the voice feel artificial, which, in conjunction with the dialogue at the end, paint a nightmarish conflict between dreams and reality.
